key_terms: The per-column structure that retrieves a document's value, the baseline for every column.
Mapping each distinct column value to a compact integer identifier that other index structures can reference.
A structure mapping each value to the documents containing it, which speeds equality filters on moderately selective columns.
A structure that speeds interval predicates such as amount between two values.
A column by which a segment's rows are physically ordered, so a filter on it can locate a contiguous document range.

worked_examples.title: Index declarations in the table config
worked_examples.interpretation: From table.json, the inverted index maps each region value to the matching document IDs, and the range index supports comparisons on amount. Both are built when the segment is created, so adding one to an existing table needs a segment reload before it takes effect. A config that lists an index is a request, not proof; confirm it in the segment metadata from the controller before claiming that a query used it.

worked_examples.title: An equality and range filter together
worked_examples.code:
SELECT
  id
FROM
  ds60_orders
WHERE
  region = 'east'
  AND amount >= 5
ORDER BY
  id
LIMIT 10
worked_examples.interpretation: The expected result is the single ID 3, because ID 1 is in east but has amount 4. Run EXPLAIN PLAN FOR on the same statement to see which filter operators Pinot chose; an inverted index filter on region and a range filter on amount should appear instead of a full scan. With three rows, timing differences are noise, so compare plans and docs-scanned counts on two separately named tables before arguing about speed.

evidence: Prepared actual Pinot Docker workshop and explicitly scoped extensions. Qualification ledger distinguishes source, native service acceptance, indexes, streaming, hybrid/upsert and multistage observations.
